text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The newspaper carried out an investigation which showed that people arrested for smuggling find high-ranking officials to help them.
- Lithuania's national basketball team got into the finals of the European basketball championship in summer in Spain after beating Switzerland 118 to 62.
- Lithuanian social democrats are against the privatisation of Butinge oil terminal.

- Nothing can stop radical tax reform, said new Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta in an interview to the newspaper. The minister added that he is a supporter of the free market economy and an opponent of subsidies.
- German concern Siemens AG denied the rumours that it intends to withdraw from Lithuania and assured it will expand its activities in the country's market.
- The heads of companies and accountants are forming queues at the Tax inspection to declare their income before March 1.

- If elections took place tomorrow, 20.4 percent would vote for the ruling Homeland Union, down by 3.5 percent since the last poll, while 11.8 percent would vote for the Centre Union, up one percent. Some 10.3 percent said they would back the former ruling Lithuanian Democratic Labour party, a leap of 4.4 percent.
- The government said its priority over the next four years is to encourage direct foreign investments and to form a favourable investment climate in the country.
